Custom tool drawer inserts from a photo

InsertCreator is a free browser editor for custom drawer organizers and tool trays. Take a top-down photo of your tools with a scale reference, check the detected outlines, and arrange fitted pockets in modular inserts. Use the editor on a computer, iPhone, iPad or Android device. No account is required, and your photos are processed locally on your device.

The editor supports Czech and English. Use the CS / EN control in the application to choose your language. Length fields support millimetres and inches; manufacturing files use millimetres.

From your tools to a printable insert

  1. Measure the drawer. Enter the usable internal width, depth and height. Check for runners, screws and any obstruction above the closed drawer.
  2. Photograph the tools. Place them separately on a contrasting surface with a ruler or A4 sheet. Keep the camera directly above the tools and the reference in the same plane. Set the scale and inspect every outline, especially dark handles, open jaws and small gaps.
  3. Design the pockets. Adjust clearance, pocket depth and finger cutouts. Move tools and modules into a layout that matches the way you work. A photograph provides an outline, so measure tool height separately.
  4. Check the design. Compare the 2D and 3D previews. Export a 1:1 PDF template and verify a known distance with a ruler. Print a small test piece to check clearance before making the complete insert.

Gridfinity 42 mm or ordinary modules

Choose ordinary drawer inserts or a Gridfinity layout based on the 42 mm grid. For example, a 5 × 4 grid occupies 210 × 168 mm before any surrounding gap. Measure the usable drawer first, then allow space for assembly and your printer's tolerances. A matching grid pitch alone does not prove that a printed part fits an existing baseplate.

You can include module joints, magnet holes and tool labels. Check magnet dimensions, joint fit and pocket clearance with a small physical sample. The export can split large modules to suit the configured print bed.

STL, 3MF, vector outlines and a 1:1 PDF

Export STL for 3D printing. Multicolour exports also provide 3MF parts; assign the required filament colours in your slicer and inspect the first layers. SVG and DXF provide outlines for further work. The 1:1 PDF helps you compare the proposed layout against the real tools before spending filament.

Print the PDF at 100% / actual size and disable “fit to page”. Measure a known dimension on paper. In your slicer, verify the model dimensions, bed placement, walls and pockets. Photo calibration, print shrinkage and tool shape can affect fit, so the preview does not replace a test print.

Your files stay under your control

Projects and the tool library are stored in your browser. Save a JSON project file to keep a backup or move your design to another device. Clearing browser storage can remove locally saved projects. Optional visitor analytics starts only after consent; declining it does not prevent design or export.
